title: Body of Christ
definition: The Body of Christ describes the Church as believers united to Christ and to one another with diverse gifts and mutual care.
summary: The Body of Christ teaches that believers are organically joined to Christ the Head and to one another as members with different functions.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the head who gives life, direction, and unity to His body.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Body of Christ describes the church as believers joined to Christ the Head and to one another as members. Scripture teaches that Christians are not isolated spiritual consumers but living parts of one body.

Every member matters, but no member is complete alone. Different gifts, weaknesses, sufferings, and callings are designed by God for mutual care and service.

Jesus gives life and direction to His body. The church is healthiest when every part depends on Him and honors the other parts He has placed there.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Pride says, 'I do not need you,' while shame says, 'You do not need me.' The body image rebukes both and gives dignity to overlooked members, including those who feel limited, wounded, or weak.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Refuse isolation and comparison. Receive help humbly, offer your gifts faithfully, and look for members of the body who need honor, encouragement, and practical support.
